Clear-sky solar radiation

Source: R/forcing-derived.R
ef_rso.Rd

Computes the clear-sky solar radiation \(R_{so}\), the solar radiation that would reach a horizontal surface under a cloudless sky, from the extraterrestrial radiation and the elevation (FAO-56). It is the reference of the cloudiness term of the net longwave radiation of the reference surface (ef_ref_net_radiation()).

Usage

ef_rso(extraterrestrial, elevation)

Arguments

extraterrestrial

Numeric. Extraterrestrial radiation \(R_a\) [MJ m-2 per day or per period], from ef_ra_daily() or ef_ra_period(). Must be finite and >= 0.

elevation

Numeric. Elevation of the site above sea level \(z\) [m], finite.

Value

A numeric vector of clear-sky radiation \(R_{so}\) in the unit of extraterrestrial [MJ m-2 per day or per period], with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim.

Details

$$R_{so} = (0.75 + 2 \times 10^{-5} z) R_a$$ (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 37 = annex 3, Eq. 3-13). FAO-56 (annex 3, after Allen, 1996) states that it is a good approximation for daily and hourly periods at elevations below 6000 m and low turbidity, obtained by linearising Beer's law with elevation for a mean sun angle of about 50 degrees. Elevations outside that range are not rejected (the bound is a validity statement, not a physical limit). The forms with turbidity and precipitable water (annex 3, Eqs. 3-14 to 3-20), for high turbidity or low sun angles, are not implemented (decision WF-12: Eq. 37 is the standard form for the reference surface; the variants serve quality control).

Missing values propagate. Negative or infinite radiation and infinite elevations raise earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status

VERIFICADA (FAO-56, chapter 3, Eq. 37; annex 3, Eq. 3-13; cases V14 and V15). The same equation is the default clear-sky radiation of the ASCE-EWRI (2005) standardized procedure for daily (Eq. 19, p. 22) and hourly periods (Eq. 47, p. 37); the report reserves the more complex forms of its Appendix D for assessing the solar radiation data.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

ASCE-EWRI (2005). The ASCE Standardized Reference Evapotranspiration Equation. Task Committee on Standardization of Reference Evapotranspiration, Environmental and Water Resources Institute of the American Society of Civil Engineers. Final report, January 2005. Published as Allen, R. G., Walter, I. A., Elliott, R. L., Howell, T. A., Itenfisu, D., Jensen, M. E., & Snyder, R. L. (Eds.), American Society of Civil Engineers, Reston, VA. doi:10.1061/9780784408056

See also

Other derived meteorological variables: ef_dewpoint(), ef_ea, ef_es(), ef_es_slope(), ef_psychrometric(), ef_ra_daily(), ef_ra_period(), ef_wind_2m()

Examples

# FAO-56 example 18 (Uccle, 100 m): Ra = 41.09 MJ m-2 d-1
ef_rso(extraterrestrial = 41.09, elevation = 100)
#> [1] 30.89968
